faq.q: Why does a sharp edge cut better?
faq.a: Pressure is force divided by area. A sharp edge has a tiny area, so the same force makes much more pressure and pushes into the material easily.
asks: Why do sharp knives cut better?

faq.q: How does a wedge push things apart?
faq.a: The sloping sides of a wedge are ramps. As it is driven forward, they push the material sideways, so a force along the wedge becomes forces across it.
asks: How does an axe split a log?

faq.q: Why is a thin wedge better than a fat one?
faq.a: A thin wedge has a long slope compared with its thickness, so it gives a bigger sideways force for each push. Its ideal mechanical advantage is its length divided by its thickness.
asks: What is the mechanical advantage of a wedge?

faq.q: Why is a wedge a simple machine?
faq.a: A wedge changes the size and direction of a force using no other parts: a small push along it makes bigger forces at right angles.
A doorstop is a wedge pushed under a door. The door presses down on the slope, and friction on the floor stops it sliding out, so the door is held.
asks: Why does a wedge hold a door open?

facts: The ideal mechanical advantage of a wedge is its length divided by its thickness at the wide end.
Wedges are among the oldest tools: stone hand axes were made over a million years ago.
